job.style: a news-style report about a real-world situation

passage: In a local chemistry lab, students observed a fascinating reaction between zinc granules and copper sulfate solution. As the reaction progressed, the blue color of the solution faded, and a reddish-brown deposit appeared on the zinc. This is a displacement reaction where zinc, being more reactive, replaces copper. Interestingly, when students performed a separate experiment heating calcium carbonate, it broke down into calcium oxide and carbon dioxide gas. Unlike physical crushing, this chemical decomposition requires energy to break internal bonds. In another corner, a student tried to balance the equation for water formation by changing the formula of water to H2O2, but the teacher corrected them, explaining that subscripts define the substance itself and cannot be altered. Finally, the class discussed food preservation. To prevent chips from turning rancid, manufacturers flush packets with nitrogen gas. This displaces oxygen, preventing the oxidation of fats. Students learned that oxidation is not just about adding oxygen; it involves the loss of electrons, which can occur even in reactions without oxygen gas. By keeping the reaction environment controlled, the mass remains conserved, and the chemical identity of the substances is preserved throughout the process.

items.evidence: This is a displacement reaction where zinc, being more reactive, replaces copper.
items.q: Why can zinc take the place of copper in copper sulfate solution?
options: Zinc is more reactive than copper
Copper is more reactive than zinc
Every metal is able to replace copper
Zinc dissolves because the solution is liquid
items.explain: Zinc is more reactive than copper, so it pushes copper out, leaving a reddish-brown deposit.

wrong.why: reverses which metal is more reactive
thinks any metal can displace any other metal
thinks the solution is just a liquid that dissolves zinc

items.evidence: Unlike physical crushing, this chemical decomposition requires energy to break internal bonds.
items.q: How is heating calcium carbonate different from crushing it into powder?
options: Heating breaks bonds to make new substances
Heating only breaks it into smaller pieces
Heating destroys mass as the gas escapes
Heating needs less energy than crushing does
items.explain: Heating breaks internal bonds, making calcium oxide and carbon dioxide; crushing only makes smaller pieces.

wrong.why: thinks decomposition is just physical breaking
thinks giving off gas lowers the total mass
mixes up which process needs energy

items.evidence: In another corner, a student tried to balance the equation for water formation by changing the formula of water to H2O2, but the teacher corrected them, explaining that subscripts define the substance itself and cannot be altered.
items.q: Why was it wrong to balance the water equation by writing H2O2?
options: Changing subscripts makes a different substance
Changing subscripts is allowed only for gases
Changing subscripts adds too many molecules
Changing subscripts must be done on both sides
items.explain: Subscripts define the substance itself, so H2O2 is no longer water.

wrong.why: thinks subscripts can sometimes be changed
thinks balancing means equal molecule counts
thinks it is fine if done evenly

items.evidence: Students learned that oxidation is not just about adding oxygen; it involves the loss of electrons, which can occur even in reactions without oxygen gas.
items.q: How can oxidation take place in a reaction with no oxygen gas?
options: A substance loses electrons in the reaction
A substance gains electrons in the reaction
A substance still reacts with traces of air
A substance is broken down by bacteria
items.explain: Oxidation means losing electrons, which can happen even without oxygen gas.

wrong.why: thinks oxidation always needs oxygen present
mixes up oxidation with bacteria spoiling food
